scope: Generic XP3 inline alternate filenames and checksum-validated folded-hash XOR resources. No original executable or DLL is executed, and no installed game bytes are included.

sources.reviewed: inline name record parser, exact/trailing-NUL lengths, next File association
Adler-32 position weighting and candidate ambiguity policy; independent single-byte histogram specialization
complete YuzuCrypt class: key folds entry hash xor seed; zero-key replacement; offset-independent XOR

implementation.inference: Unique bias requires two distinct non-identity entry hashes and exact Adler-32 candidate compatibility. A zero-domain replacement is learned only from actual checksum-validated zero-domain bytes. All protected opens verify the complete logical bytes, including authenticated plain bootstrap exceptions.
implementation.limits: 64MiB total inference sample bytes, at most 32 samples; shared 64MiB input limit and cancellation; runtime per-entry/resident decode limits still apply.
implementation.ownership: SourceArchive and AssetReader resources, independent of the KiriKiri VM; capability-scoped mount context carries archive parameters. No game-name cipher selection or title key catalogue.
implementation.name_namespace: Verified inline preferred names take precedence over same-name plain-index fallback records. Native info-token aliases and original record IDs are retained; multiple inline candidates or alias/name conflicts fail. Original fallback bytes remain readable by archive record ID, with shadowed IDs recorded on the visible preferred resource.
implementation.namespace_evidence_scope: The pinned parser defines alternate_name as preferred_name. Inline hash/MD5 relationships and separate plain versus inline startup records were observed in the owner container. Priority of that proven logical namespace over a colliding ordinary-index fallback is an explicit CrySirror archive policy; this audit does not claim a reverse-engineered native executable sort routine.

fixtures: Self-authored synthetic inline indexes, mixed plain/encrypted entries, independently computed checksums, zero-domain, wrong-profile and corrupt-later-entry cases. Owner archive test is ignored by default and explicitly selected at runtime.
